Oh, and Derrick Henry will look to run all over his former team in the Tennessee Titans . That's a must-watch revenge game. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on Tee Higgins at +175 and tight end Harold Fannin Jr . at +235. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 4. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a tight end who looked incredible last week in his 2026 debut. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. 1. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (+160) The Las Vegas Raiders have a massive matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs this week. The Raiders are off to a surprising 3-0 start, although we can't ignore the fact that they've played the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL up to this point, as their first three opponents have won one game combined. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut last week against the New Orleans Saints , and he looked magnificent. He caught a game-high 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in a 35-27 win, and will be important if the Raiders want to score an upset victory over their rivals. With how good Bowers looked last week, I'll sprinkle on him again in this spot as Kirk Cousins ' new clear-cut "WR1." 2. Bills RB James Cook (-140) James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is one of the best running backs in the NFL, and he's on a bit of a heater right now. He rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 vs. the Detroit Lions , and then 24 times for 154 yards and another touchdown last week against the Los Angeles Chargers . Now, the flailing New England Patriots come to town, and they are missing two important defenders in Christian Barmore and Christian Gonzalez . They lost by 29 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, and I'm sure Joe Brady and the Bills want to do something similar to the team that won their division last year. A -140 price isn't value, but I can tell you I was surprised by this listing. 3. Vikings RB Aaron Jones (-160) Like James Cook, this line doesn't offer much value. But consider that the Miami Dolphins have allowed six touchdowns to running backs through three games. The Minnesota Vikings are favored by double-digits over Miami, which makes sense because the Dolphins just lost De'Von Achane for the year, while Brian Flores is going to look to DESTROY his former team from a defensive standpoint. That means Aaron Jones is going to get plenty of touches. He hasn't scored since Week 1, but will in Week 4. 4. Jets RB Braelon Allen (+115) I was a fan of Braelon Allen in the 2024 draft process because he's big at 6-foot-1, 235 pounds, and was the youngest player in the entire class. He actually racked up 482 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns as a rookie, but an injury held him to four games played last year. Now, he's making his third career start with Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury. When the New York Jets get in the red zone against the Chicago Bears , Frank Reich is going to call his number. 5. Saints RB Alvin Kamara (+135) (Monday) This game is on Monday night, but I had to mention it. The Saints are hosting the Atlanta Falcons in the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth Game," where the Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina. The legendary Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the opening drive of the game, which set the tone for an emotional 23-3 Saints victory. I can't imagine what the environment will be like on Monday night. Travis Etienne is out with a hamstring injury, opening the door for franchise legend Alvin Kamara . He's not as productive as he used to be, but it makes too much sense for him to score in this game. Bonus: Ravens RB Derrick Henry 2 TDs (+250) Derrick Henry faces the team that selected him No. 45 overall in the 2016 NFL Draft this Sunday. Henry and the Titans didn't have some dramatic breakup, but Henry wanted to win football games and the Titans were about to suffer an embarrassing fall to the bottom of the league, so a mutual parting of ways made sense. It used to be a debate if Henry was a future Hall of Famer. Not anymore. The ageless wonder leads the NFL with 3,817 rushing yards and 38 rushing touchdowns since signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Those are more rushing yards and more rushing touchdowns than the entire Titans offense since he left. Derrick Henry to find the end zone at -210 is probably a parlay leg, but what about two touchdowns at +250? He's averaging two touchdowns a game this year as it is! Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. Winnipeg Blue Bombers vs. Edmonton Elks Winnipeg +4.5, -105 @ BetMGM Edmonton has been one of the CFL's biggest surprises this season, but this spread feels a bit too generous toward the home side. The Blue Bombers have had extra time to regroup following last week's victory over Ottawa and remain one of the league's most disciplined teams on both sides of the football. Winnipeg's defense has consistently limited explosive plays, which is critical against an Edmonton offense led by Cody Fajardo that thrives on sustaining long drives. For what it's worth, the Blue Bombers have allowed the fourth-most yards per game in 2026, and they'll be facing an Edmonton team that has generated the third-most yards on offense. Even if the Elks ultimately protect home field, Winnipeg has the experience and defensive playmakers to keep this game within one possession, not to mention an offense led by star-caliber players such as Zach Collaros and Brady Oliveira . Back the Blue Bombers to cover in this case. Hamilton Tiger-Cats vs. Toronto Argonauts Under 59.5 points, -105 @ FanDuel This matchup has all the ingredients of a shootout, but the total set at nearly 60 points simply looks too high here. Sure, Hamilton is coming off an emotional comeback victory over Saskatchewan, while Toronto returns home looking to bounce back after a lopsided defeat. And yes, both offenses possess enough firepower to move the ball consistently, and neither defense has been particularly reliable at preventing explosive plays throughout the season. However, the Tiger-Cats are averaging just 23.7 points per game this season, the second-worst mark in the CFL, and they've been forced to improvise under center due to the absence of Bo Levi Mitchell (ankle), while star wideout Shemar Bridges (hip) has yet to play in 2026. The Roughriders remain one of the CFL's most complete teams when Trevor Harris is protected, and their balanced offensive attack prevents defenses from focusing on any one playmaker. While the Lions have shown flashes offensively, especially now that Nathan Rourke is back under center, the reality is that the team has struggled to consistently put together four-quarter performances, leaving the door open for Saskatchewan to capitalize. The Roughriders also possess one of the league's more physical defenses, a unit capable of generating pressure without excessive blitzing and forcing opponents into difficult second-and-long situations. While the Lions lead the CFL in yards allowed per game by a wide margin (339.6), it's hard to see their defense controlling the game against Saskatchewan's elite offense. By Zachary Cohen - September 19, 2026 79084 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 2 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 2 NFL best bets and Week 2 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Philadelphia Eagles at Tennessee Titans – 1:00 pm ET Last week, Barkley rushed for 83 yards on only 15 carries in a win over the Commanders. Now, the star faces a Titans team that allowed 142 yards on 32 carries against the Jets duo of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen. In that game, Tennessee’s Rush EPA/Play Allowed was -0.038, which was right around the -0.043 mark the team posted in 2025. All offseason long, we talked about Robert Saleh shaping up this defense, but there is a chance he won’t be successful in doing so. That said, this might just be a strong matchup for an elite rusher. Barkley is averaging 96.9 rushing yards per game in his last 30 games, and he has rushed for at least 78 yards in five of his last six games. Also, since signing with the Eagles, Barkley is averaging 100.4 rushing yards per game when Philly is favored by between 5.5 and 8 points. I just don’t see any reason he can’t get going in this game, and I’ll throw out the fact that the game script could really favor him. If the Eagles go up early, they’ll begin to rely on the run. Bet: Saquon Barkley Over 75.5 Rushing Yards (-135) & Alt Rushing Yards 100+ (+233 – 0.25 units) Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears – 1:00 pm ET I tweeted during last week’s game that I can’t understand how Wentz is the backup over JJ McCarthy, but that’s neither here nor there. Wentz went on to do just fine in a win over the Packers, and I don’t see the Vikings being shy about throwing the ball here. With the Bears having put 59 points on the Panthers, there’s just no way of standing a chance against them without making plays in the passing game. And if Bryce Young can go for 361 passing yards against this defense, you’d think Wentz can reach 225 with all of the weapons he has at his disposal. Also, the absence of Jordan Mason only makes it more likely that Kevin O’Connell will let Wentz cook — even if he’s doing it with a microwave. Wentz only threw for 133 yards in relief of an injured Kyler Murray lat week, but he also threw for at least 236 yards in three of his final four appearances in 2025. Two of those three games featured him throwing for over 300 yards. I’m not sure the result of this game will be pretty for Minnesota, but I see Wentz putting up a pretty decent yardage total. I actually really wanted to get more aggressive with this, but the pricing wasn’t great. Bet: Carson Wentz Over 224.5 Passing Yards (+127) Jacksonville Jaguars at Denver Broncos – 4:05 pm ET Is this a massive overreaction from Week 1? While the Jaguars absolutely pounded the Browns, the Broncos looked lousy in a 31-10 loss against the Chiefs. However, looking back to a year ago, Denver was a better football team than Jacksonville. Also, the Broncos had a better offseason than the Jaguars. So, while things did look ugly offensively last week, I’m chalking it up to a weird game. I don’t think anyone should be sounding the alarms on Davis Webb running the offense, and I feel good about Denver bouncing back at home. Under Sean Payton, the Broncos are 4-1 both straight-up and against the spread in home games with totals of 45.5 or higher. Denver also happens to be 6-1 both SU and ATS after scoring 14 or fewer points in its previous game. Those trends support a much better performance from the Broncos — and especially the Denver offense — in Week 2. It’s also pretty easy to envision the Broncos corners enjoying a matchup with an average group of receivers. Denver can also put some pressure on Trevor Lawrence, and I trust the defense to do well against a shaky Jacksonville backfield. On top of all of that, the Broncos look rather sharp here. While most of the action on our VSiN betting splits pages shows public faith in Jacksonville, the line hasn’t budged. Literally, 900 ways. Legalization provides opportunities for sportsbooks to get creative and, boy, have they figured out a way to entice people from all walks of life. I wrote about the prop phenomenon years ago. Here are my five favorite bets for Sunday. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . First quarter Over/Under 8.5 points This wager is nothing new to loyal readers. I love shorting offense and banking on defense early in Super Bowls. Hell, Tom Brady never engineered a first-quarter touchdown drive in nine Super Bowls with the Patriots. Nerves should certainly be a thing for both Sam Darnold and Drake Maye , and I’ll be rooting for 0-0, 3-0, 3-3, 6-0, 7-0 or 8-0. Anything 9 or higher is a loss. PICK: First quarter Under 8.5 points scored (-115) Longest field goal Under 49.5 yards Sure, both kickers are weapons, but these coaching staffs are rather aggressive on fourth-and-3 or shorter. That’s because Mike Macdonald and Mike Vrabel trust their defenses coming back the other way. Don’t be surprised when one of these teams passes up a 50-yarder to leave the offense on the field. If somebody drills a long one heading into the half, so be it. PICK: Longest field goal Under 49.5 yards (-110) Drake Maye Under 37.5 rushing yards Does anybody like the Under here? The first number I saw, this prop was 28.5, and now we’re almost 10 yards higher. Alrighty then. It’s easy to peep playoff box scores and see Maye’s 66 yards against Los Angeles and 65 against Denver. However, you can’t ignore the 10 rushing yards versus Houston. I expect Seattle’s stingy defense to account for Maye and limit his breakouts. PICK: Drake Maye Under 37.5 rushing yards (-105) Mack Hollins Under 2.5 catches Wise guys popped this in Vegas at -110 and -130, but I still think it’s good to about -160. Anything higher, it’s a pass. Caesars is out to -200. Woof. Hollins was a popular target for Maye during the regular season until he suffered an abdomen injury in Week 16 at Baltimore. He was activated for the AFC Championship and caught two passes against the big, bad Denver defense. His life doesn’t get any easier against a loaded Seattle secondary. PICK: Mack Hollins Under 2.5 catches (-155) Rashid Shaheed MVP Now we’re gambling. I made this full-unit bet expecting to lose, though it’s easy for me to make a case for Seattle’s Swiss army knife. Shaheed is a speedster that’s no stranger to home-run plays. We saw him blow by defenders and score an 87-yard touchdown pass earlier this season. He also returns kicks and punts, so he’ll touch the ball in high-leverage situations. And who knows, maybe Klint Kubiak will use Shaheed in the running game. FanDuel is offering 45-1 — the best price by far — and I think it’s well worth a bet. But with Kenneth Walker III gone, a rookie running back in his place and a new offensive coordinator, there will be hiccups and growing pains in this game. Tight ends saw a lot of success against Seattle’s defense last season, and Henry was one of the best against zone schemes (which the Seahawks often run). Doubs and Brown will be the superstars in the passing game, but Henry is the glue that will move the chains and keep drives moving. By Adam Burke - September 19, 2026 43890 X Facebook Email NFL Player Props A lot of the usual suspects had big games in Week 1, but there were others who stood out that got off to better starts than expected. Every week gives us a chance to analyze snap counts, usage rates, targets, carries, and all of the other prop betting options that are available. Dustin Swedelson already gave us some of his favorite player prop bets that lined up with our OptaAI projections. We also have some awesome tools here at VSiN to help with your prop betting picks, including our OptaAI NFL Player Prop Projections , exclusively available to our Pro Subscribers . Whether you use them as confirmation of a play that you already like or scan through to find the biggest edges, it is just another weapon in your arsenal against the sportsbooks while trying to build up that bankroll. I also have my First Touchdown Scorer predictions posted for this week, which includes a tracking spreadsheet of 1st TDs for every team and each individual player. As always, shop around for these Week 2 NFL Player Props. Lines are as of 6:30 p.m. ET on Friday, September 18 and are from DraftKings. Here are my favorite Week 2 NFL Player Prop Bets: Caleb Douglas (MIA) Over 38.5 Receiving Yards (-109) Perhaps last week was a fluke, as Douglas, the rookie wideout from Texas Tech, had five catches for 94 yards, but it’s pretty clear that he’s high up on the pecking order. The Dolphins had 56 offensive snaps and Douglas was out there for 51 of them. Only Malik Washington (55) had more snaps outside of the offensive linemen and QB Malik Willis. So, Douglas is going to be out there with chances. The game state should also help here, as the Dolphins project to trail throughout the game again, and probably by even more than they did last week against the Raiders. Douglas didn’t have any drops on seven targets and caught five passes for 59 yards before contact. With the 49ers probably playing soft zone in the second half, Douglas should have some room to work. Our OptaAI projections have Douglas down for 48.19 receiving yards. Jonathon Brooks (CAR) Under 21.5 Rushing Yards (-108) While the Panthers were busy giving up a million points and a million yards to the Bears, we got a glimpse of how the playing time might go at the running back position. Even with ample opportunities to get Brooks, who missed the entire 2025 season and only had nine carries in 2024, some reps and some time with the starting offense, it didn’t happen. Brooks had just 13 snaps and only four carries. He did have an explosive play in the passing game and maybe that will get him some more playing time in third-down situations, but Chuba Hubbard had a 70% snap share and it’s pretty clear that Dave Canales and Brad Idzik have more trust in the more proven player. That may change as the season goes along, but this looks like Hubbard’s backfield right now. Our OptaAI projections dramatically disagree with 44.11 rushing yards for Brooks this week, so we’ll see if I win or the machines win. Matt Gay (LV) Over 5.5 Kicking Points (-119) Klint Kubiak is a very sharp offensive mind and it’s no secret as to why he got this job. He’s there to help Ashton Jeanty and Fernando Mendoza develop. Unfortunately, he’ll be without Brock Bowers again this week, but the Raiders should be able to put themselves in scoring situations, even against a better team in the Chargers. The Raiders gained 50+ yards on four of their first six drives, including a 93-yard TD drive. But, they slowed down the pace and went into a bit of a shell with the lead over their final five possessions, with three of them going for negative yards. I don’t think Kubiak wanted to show too much in a game that they had in hand. Gay, who was 2-for-2 on FGs and 3-for-3 on PATs, gets to kick inside again here at SoFi Stadium and he’s kicked at a 91.1% success rate in domes in his career, going 51-of-56.
